advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make run_differs' observation `mode` fall back to "live" (not "") when target_mode is None, matching reconcile.py's `target_mode.value if target_mode else "live"`.
evidence: run_differs.py:271-274 comment: "mirroring reconcile.py's ``target_mode.value if target_mode else \"live\"``"
advisory.finding: In run_differs the observation `mode` is derived as `str(getattr(_target_mode, 'value', _target_mode) or '')`, which falls back to an empty string when `ctx.target_mode` is None; the inline comment claims it mirrors reconcile.py's `target_mode.value if target_mode else "live"`, but reconcile.py falls back to "live", not "". This divergence means a pass with target_mode=None records mode="" in the Observation (and its fingerprint) where the canonical convention is "live".
scenarios: A reconcile pass where ctx.target_mode is None/absent: the Observation records mode="" instead of "live", producing a fingerprint that will never match reconcile.py's own live-fallback semantics.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `mode = str(getattr(_target_mode, "value", _target_mode) or "")` with a fallback to "live", e.g. `mode = str(getattr(_target_mode, "value", _target_mode) or "live")`, or explicitly `"live" if _target_mode is None else str(getattr(_target_mode, "value", _target_mode))`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that plan_pass(mutations=[]) returns a valid Observation and an empty plans tuple.
evidence: ticket_planner.py: `grouped: dict[str, list[Any]] = defaultdict(list)` then `for target in sorted(grouped)` — with mutations=[] this loop yields no plans
ABSENCE: every test passes _mutations(...) (four mutations); no test calls plan_pass(mutations=[]) to assert observation is still built and plans == ()
advisory.finding: plan_pass with an empty mutations sequence is untested. The added grouping logic (defaultdict + sorted(grouped)) yields zero TicketPlans while build_observation still produces a valid observation; this boundary of the new pure function has no coverage.
scenarios: A reconcile pass that finalizes zero mutations (nothing to change) still attaches a shadow observation with an empty ticket_plans tuple
advisory.suggested_fix: Add test asserting `obs, plans = _plan_pass(..., mutations=[])` gives `plans == ()` and `obs.version.fingerprint` is a non-empty string equal to a fresh empty-mutations build (determinism).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting two TicketPlans differing only in payload are unequal yet both hashable (e.g. insertable into a set).
evidence: ABSENCE: test_provider_payload_extension_stays_open asserts payload values are visible but never constructs two plans differing only by payload to assert inequality, and no test inserts a TicketPlan into a set/dict to prove __hash__ works with a dict payload
dropped.finding: The TicketPlan __eq__/__hash__ identity split (payload included in __eq__ but excluded from __hash__) is newly added behavior that no test exercises. Two TicketPlans identical in all hashable fields but differing only in payload must compare unequal, yet both must remain hashable (usable in a set/dict). A regression that either dropped payload from __eq__ or added it to __hash__ (making payload dicts unhashable) would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor accidentally adds payload to __hash__, raising TypeError on set insertion
A refactor drops payload from __eq__, silently deduplicating plans that differ only by provider payload
dropped.suggested_fix: Construct plan_a and plan_b identical except payload={'k':1} vs {'k':2}; assert plan_a != plan_b, assert hash(plan_a) == hash(plan_b), and assert {plan_a, plan_b} succeeds (no TypeError).
